newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market opening report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market opening report.

text.p: South African shares started firm on Monday, riding high on Wall Street's positive gains on Friday and on comments by central bank governor Chris Stals that an interest rate cut was likely later this year.
Dealers said the rate cut talk was positive news for a market which had been largely subdued for the past few weeks.
"The market is looking quite strong with the Dow having closed up on Friday and sentiment is positive," a dealer said.
Producer price inflation figures which are due for release on Tuesday at 0900 GMT were seen coming off from recent highs.
"With regards to inflation we expect PPI figures...to come back.

"Our expectations are at the lower end of the market around about 9.1/9.2 percent from 9.6 percent which should add emphasis to the expectations that a sooner rather than later cut in interest rates will be on the cards," James Scott, an equities trader at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
Dealers said trade was active with 93 million rand worth of shares changing hands in first 10 minutes and the suprise leap in May official reserves last week also added to the climb.
"When the reserve figures came out that was really the turn of the sentiment," Scott said.
The financial index reacted sharply to Stals' comments and surged to new highs. It soared 90.9 points to a fresh high of 9,710.2.
The industrial index added 27.1 points to 8,504.3 points, the gold index was up 1.2 points to 1,1768 points and the all-share index gained 25.0 points to a new record high at 7,287.2 points.
